I don't have any notes for you yet. My two attempts to fetch the source pages failed: the first stopped on a bug in my code, and then I hit the limit on research tool calls for this turn. So I haven't read any commentary on Psalm 134.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written notes from memory.

If you ask me to continue in a new message, I'll fetch these pages and write the verse-by-verse notes from them:

- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com (Guzik on Psalm 134), the biblehub.com commentary pages for vv. 1–3 (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes, Matthew Henry) and the preceptaustin.org page on Psalm 134
- **Protestant traditions:** spurgeon.org or ccel.org (Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*), wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), plus any Psalm 134 material on ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, lcms.org and 1517.org
- **Other views:** netbible.org's translator notes (for example on "by night" and "lift up your hands"), newadvent.org (Augustine on this Psalm, numbered 133 in the Septuagint) and oca.org (Orthodox use of the Psalm)

I'll also note which of these questions the sources don't cover. For example, I may not find any real Protestant disagreement or any prosperity or word-of-faith teaching on this short Psalm.
